take:
Most of these 107 posts treat Claude Code as a harness people customize for whole jobs. Website builds are a common demo: a CLAUDE.md of design rules, the frontend-design skill and a loop where the agent screenshots and critiques its own UI ([website recipe](/e/DW_8FsslNJi)), or a DESIGN.md pasted in as a baseline ([awesome-design-md](/e/DW-ag7St6UM)). Others launch Meta ads through an Ads MCP ([ads pipeline](/e/DcR6KUyPC0n)) or turn 36 YouTube videos into a linked wiki ([knowledge base](/e/DWzPgGhiTcR)).

Repeated habits come largely from Anthropic's Boris Cherny: 3-5 parallel git worktrees, plan mode for complex tasks, and a CLAUDE.md updated after every correction ([team tips](/e/DVQ5o6YDfsp)). A counter-current says less is more: the "simple mode" strips the system prompts and Anthropic found the model slightly smarter without them ([simple mode](/e/DcMSk7Rxcdu)), and one creator urges auditing stale rules written for older models ([setup purge](/e/Dbhuaw7Pk4u)). The [Claude Code mastery guide](/guides/claude-code-mastery) collects these patterns.

Cost and limits are the main complaints. Creators reroute the harness to OpenRouter when they hit usage caps, accepting weaker tool use from small free models ([OpenRouter swap](/e/DW6yhr6CHoP)), and from June 15 `claude -p` and Agent SDK runs were billed per token outside plan limits ([billing split](/e/DYXWNTERFhZ)). One caption cites an analysis of 6,852 sessions claiming thinking depth fell 67% ([session data](/e/DW6wPs2DQuK)); it is a single unverified report.

Codex shows up in 9 of these posts, usually as a second model that audits Claude Code's output ([Codex audit](/e/DV3lILoEfzS)). Playwright appears in 8, mostly so the agent can check its own render ([design stack](/e/DbLuwUVlE9Z)); Obsidian and ChatGPT each appear in 7, with Obsidian serving as the memory vault ([agentic OS](/e/DXYSxNLpIAY)). Cursor appears in 6. Many posts are comment-gated teasers with little method shown. The audience is mostly terminal-comfortable builders, though a non-coder uses it to map their own app's bugs ([architecture map](/e/DYP-TkppmPM)).
